p01.s01: Detecting lead ions rapidly in drinking water remains a practical challenge.
p01.s02: We demonstrate a low-cost and easy to use colorimetric sensor based on a chelating membrane.
p01.s03: The data were collected from 36 water samples in three cities.
p01.s04: The limit of detection is 0.8 µg/L [3], which is lower than values reported previously (Fig. 2).
p01.s05: Samples did not require pretreatment, and the assay can be completed in 12 min.
p01.s06: These results may suggest that the method could be applied in resource-limited settings, although field validation is still needed.
